<a> and <ommawh> written as one word: who is restless or naughty, said of a child

terms: where he lives/whereabouts/place where there is
definition: <a> and <omna> written as one word: the place where someone or something is or lives; before a noun, the place where such people or things are

terms: so that there is/in order to have
definition: <a>, <om> and <nading> written as one word: for there to be, so that something exists or is kept, as in {lungmuanna aomnading}, to keep the peace

terms: so that there is/in order that there be
definition: <aom>, there is, with a shortened form of <nading>, in order to, written as one word: so that there may be

terms: there is no longer/be no more
definition: <a> and <omnawnlo> written as one word: there is no longer any, or the one that no longer has or is
<a>, <omnawn> be any more and the negative <loh> written as one word, the form used before <ciangin>, <manin> and <nadingin>: no longer being there, so that there is no more of it
<a> and <omngei> written as one word: has been or has lived somewhere before, has existed before; {aomngei nailo} is that has never been

terms: the man who is/the man who lives
definition: <a> and <ompa> written as one word: the man who is or lives in a place
<a>, <om>, be, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: the one that is there, or the fact that something is or stays, as the topic of the sentence
<aom> and <phial> written as one word, followed by <zongin>: even if there is, even if there should be
<a> and <ompih> written as one word: who lives or stays with someone, the person one lives with
<a> and <omsa>, already there, written as one word: that which already exists, those who are already there
<a> and <omsam> written as one word: there are, to be sure; usually before <hang> or <hangin>, although, granting a point before a contrast
<a> and <omsuak>, stay on, written as one word: go on staying in a place, in the articles mostly in a country after a visa has run out
<aom>, he is there, and <sung>, during, written as one word, mostly followed by <in>: while he or she was in a place
<a> and <omte> written as one word: those who are or live in a place or state; {gamdang ah aomte} is those who are abroad
<a> and <omteng> written as one word: all those who are in a place, everything that is there
<a> and <omthei> written as one word: can be or can happen; {aomthei zelzel} is it happens again and again
<a> and <omtheih> written as one word; <aomtheih nadingin> is so that there may be, so that one can stay

terms: so that there may be/so that one can stay
definition: <aomtheih>, be able to be, and <nadingin>, in order to: placed after the thing wanted, as <bitna>, safety, so that there may be that thing; after a place with <ah>, so that someone can stay there
<a> and <omzawh> written as one word: the time that he, she or it has been in a place or state, followed by a length of time; also since something came to be there

terms: its condition/his behaviour/the way it is
definition: <a>, his, her or its, and <omzia>, condition or way of being, written as one word: how a person or thing is, looks or behaves

terms: even if there is/those who also are
definition: <aom>, there is, and <zong>, also or even, written as one word: even when there is, or those who are there as well
hand over or entrust to someone, especially give over to God or set apart as holy; <ki-ap> is dedicated or devoted
a male animal, <pa> with the prefix <a>; the opposite is <anu>, a female one
<a>, his or her, and <pa>, father, written as one word: the father of the person spoken of, often paired with <anu>, the mother, as in <anu apa>, the parents; not the male animal of the other sense
<a> and <paai> written as one word, in {nau apaai}: she is pregnant, her being with child
only in the pair {asum apaai}, money and means: the funds and goods that a work needs; the second word is that of {sum leh paai}, money and goods, not the verb <paai>, throw
<a>, <paai>, carry a child, and <lam>, the fact, written as one word after <nau>: the fact that she is pregnant
<apaai>, she is pregnant, and <zawh>, after, since, written as one word, in {nau apaaizawh} before a number of months: the time since she became pregnant
<a> and <paak>, flower, written as one word: its flower, the flower of; before <hun> its flowering, as in {apaak hun}, the time when it blooms
<a> and <paam> written as one word, second half of the pairs <akiim apaam>, all around it, and {aveng apaam}, the neighbours
<a> and <paang> written as one word: his, her or their cheek, mostly of a cheek that is slapped
<a> and <pahtawi> written as one word: he honors, the one who honors or is to be honored; {apahtawi taak} is worthy of honor
<a> and <pahtawina> written as one word: their honoring of someone, the honor given
<a> and <pai> written as one word: he or they go, or the one who goes
<a>, <pai>, go, and <ciang>, when, written as one word and often followed by <in>: when he, she or they go or walk
<a>, <pai>, go, and <ding> written as one word: he or she will go, the one who is to go, or his or her going; {apaiding phallo} is not allow to go
<a> and <paih>, throw away, written as one word: they threw it away, what was thrown away
<a> and <paihkhiat> written as one word, before a noun: that someone has thrown away or let out
<a> and <paihsak> written as one word: who threw away or dumped something that belongs to another, or what was thrown away

terms: intend to throw away/try to dump
definition: <a>, <paih>, throw away, and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: he plans to throw it away, or the one who tried to throw it away
<a> and <paikawm> written as one word: while he is going, as he goes; usually followed by <in>
<a> and <paikhawm> written as one word: they went together, or those who go together
<apai>, the one who goes, and <khempeuh>, all, written as one word: everyone who goes or comes, every vehicle that passes
<a> and <paikhia> written as one word: he went out, the one or the thing that goes out

terms: be due to leave/be about to depart/will go out
definition: <apaikhia>, he or it goes out, with <ding>, will, written as one word: that is about to leave, said often of a train or vehicle due to set off
<a> and <paikhial> written as one word: he or they go astray, or the one who has gone wrong
<a> and <paikhiat> written as one word: he or she goes out or leaves; {apaikhiat laitak} is just as he was leaving
<apaikhiat> and <ding> written as one word: his or her going out that is still to come; with <ciangin>, when about to leave
<apaikhiat>, he or she leaves, and <ma>, before, written as one word and followed by <in>: before he, she or it leaves
<a> and <paikhiatna> written as one word: the leaving of a person or a train, or the place from which it set out
<a> and <paikhiatpih> written as one word: he, she or they go out taking someone along

terms: be about to leave/try to go out
definition: <a>, <paikhiat>, go out, and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: he or it was about to leave or tried to get away
<a> and <paikhit> written as one word: after he or she has gone, or after a time or distance has passed; mostly before <ciangin>
<a> and <paikhop> written as one word: they go along together, mostly before <laitak>, while
<a> and <paikik> written as one word: he or they go back, it comes back

terms: be going/be on the way/be travelling
definition: <a>, <pai> and <lai> written as one word: while still going, or the one who is on the way; of electricity, be running
<a>, <pai> and <laitak> written as one word: at the very time he, she or it was going or travelling
<a> and <pailam> written as one word: that someone or something goes or comes, the fact of having gone; {apailam in} is on going, on the way there
<a>, <pai>, go, and <leh>, when, written as one word: when or as he or she went, followed by what was found or what happened there
<a> and <pailoh> written as one word: he does not come, or of water it does not flow; used before words such as <ciangin>
<a> and <paina> written as one word: the place or way where someone goes, or his going; {apaina peuhah} is wherever she goes
<a>, <pai>, go, and <nading>, for, written as one word: where someone or something is going, the place or way to be gone to
<a> and <painop> written as one word: they want to go, mostly as {apainop mahmahna mun}, a place people very much like to visit
<a> and <painopna> written as one word: the place where he or she wants to go

terms: want to go/who wants to go
definition: <a> and <painuam> written as one word: he wants to go, or the one who wants to go

terms: the man who went/the one who goes
definition: <a> and <paipa> written as one word: the man who went or who is walking along
<a> and <paipai>, keep going, written as one word: he, she or it is going along, is on the move; {apaipai laitak in} is while it was going along

terms: be already moving/be on its way
definition: <a>, <paipai>, keep going, and <ta>, now, written as one word: it is already moving along
<a> and <paipak> written as one word: he or she went out for a short while

terms: the one who goes/those who went
definition: <apai>, the one who goes, and the topic marker <pen>, written as one word: as for the one who went, or as for his going
<a> and <paiphei>, go across, written as one word: he or she goes over toward a place or person, or the one that is going across
<a> and <paipih> written as one word: he, she or they took someone or something along to a place; also the one taken along or the one who takes

terms: intend to go/be about to go
definition: <a> and <paisawm> written as one word: who was planning to go or was on the way to a place
<a> and <paisuk> written as one word: that goes down, of a vehicle or a traveller heading down to a lower place; {apaisuk apaito} is those going down and those going up
<a> and <paite> written as one word: the people who go or travel; {khetawh apaite} are those going on foot, pedestrians
<a> and <paithei> written as one word: he or they can go, or the one who can go or walk

terms: be able to go/be able to come
definition: <a> and <paitheih> written as one word: that he, she or they can go; mostly in {apaitheih nadingin}, so that they can go
<a> and <paito> written as one word: the one going up, of travellers and vehicles on the way up to a place; {apaisuk apaito} are those going down and those going up
<a> and <paizia> written as one word: the way it goes, how a thing proceeds or is done
<a>, <pa>, father, and <kik>, again, written as one word: his or her stepfather
<a> and <palsat> written as one word: he breaks a law or rule, or the one who breaks it
<a> and <pam> written as one word: the place beside it; paired as <akiim apam>, {agei apam} and <aveng apam>, all around, the neighbours

terms: a little way off/close by/just beside
definition: <apam>, the place beside it, and <deuh>, somewhat, written as one word: a short distance to the side, near by
<a> and <pan>, from, written as one word after a noun or a time word: from that place or time on; {ka neu apan} is since I was small
<a> with <pan>, the form of <pang>, take part or take a side, written as one word: one who takes part; {apan pihnuam} is one who wants to join in and help
<a>, his or her, with {paneu}, the younger brother of a father, written as one word: his or her father's younger brother
<pang>, side, with the prefix <a> written as one word: the side of the thing named before it, as in {inn apang}, the side of a house
the verb <pang> with the prefix <a> written as one word, after <ma>: <ma apang> is who takes an active part in a cause or works for it
<a> and <pangkhat> written as one word: one side of a house, a box or a road
<apang>, the side, with <lam>, direction, written as one word: the side of a thing such as a road, a river or a vehicle; {apanglam ah} is to the side
plural with <te>, used to address unfaithful people; the build of the word is not confirmed
<apang>, its side, and <teng>, all, written as one word after a noun: the side or edge of a house, road or river along its length
<a> and <pankhia> written as one word: the one who began a thing, who started or founded it
<a> and <panmun> written as one word: his or her position or office; {apanmun pan khawl} is step down from office
<a> and <panpih> written as one word: who supports; {apanpih mi} and {apanpih te} are the supporters of someone
<apanpih> and <ding> written as one word: who will help or support, to help them
<a> and <panpihna> written as one word: his, her or their support, the help that someone gives
<a> and <pantah> written as one word: he or she brings up, the one who raises a child or an animal
<a>, <pa> and <pen> written as one word: his, her or their father, as the one the sentence is about
<a> and <papi> written as one word: the man of a couple, the husband, set beside <azi>, his wife
a home of several rooms inside a larger building, or the building itself
<a> and <party> written as one word: his, her or their political party, or the party as against the candidate
<a> and <pasal> written as one word: her husband, the husband of the woman spoken of
<apasal>, her husband, with the marker <in> of the doer, written as one word: her husband, as the one who acts
placed after a time or place word: starting from, since; used like <akipan>
<a> and <pat> written as one word: its beginning; {apat pan atawp dong} is from the beginning to the end
<a> and <patau> written as one word: he is or they are alarmed or afraid of something, or one who is alarmed
<apa> and <tawh> written as one word: together with his or her father
<a> and <pate> written as one word: {apu apate} is his forefathers and {anu apate} is his parents
<a> and <patkhiat> written as one word: the one who started it, what he began or founded
<a> and <patna> written as one word: the beginning, its start
<apat>, the beginning, and <pan>, from, written as one word; {apatpan atawpdong} is from beginning to end
<a> and <pattah> written as one word: he or they trained, the ones they trained, in the news said of training an armed group
<a> and <pattahsa> written as one word: the one whom he has brought up or trained
<a> and <pau>, speech, written as one word: what a person is saying, or the way he speaks
<a> and <pau>, speak, written as one word: he speaks, and the one who speaks
<a> and <pauthei> written as one word: one who can speak a language, he can speak
<pawl>, group or kind, with the prefix <a>; doubled as {apawl apawl} or {apawl pawl} it means of every kind, in every way
<pawl>, group, with the prefix <a>: the people who belong with someone, his group or allies, in {leh apawl te} after the name of a person, country or body
{a pawl}, a group or kind, with the place marker <ah>; the doubled {apawl apawlah} means in every kind of
placed after a noun: of every sort, kind by kind; <pawlpawl> with the prefix <a>
<pawl>, group or kind, doubled, with the prefix <a> and the plural suffix <te>; follows a noun, every kind of it, {ahoih na apawlpawlte} is every good work
<a> and <pawlpi>, church, written as one word: his, her or their church or congregation
{a pawl}, a group or kind, with the plural <te>; the doubled {apawl apawlte} means every kind of
after a name and <leh>, and: {a pawlte} written as one word, the people who are with that person or body, his group, delegation or allies; not the doubled {apawl apawlte}, every kind
<ap>, hand over or entrust, and <ding> written as one word: to hand over, to entrust; {ki apding} is to give oneself up, to surrender
<a> and <peem> written as one word: one who has moved into a place that is not home and lives there
<a> and <peeng> written as one word: the twins, children born together at one birth
<a> and <peh>, bite, written as one word: of an animal, bite or maul a person; before a noun, the one that bites
<a> with {pehlup}, the form of <petlum>, bite to death, used when the clause describes a noun or stands before a word such as <khitciangin>: of a crocodile or a shark, the one it bit to death
<a> and <pei>, wheel, written as one word: the wheel or wheels of a car, train or aircraft

terms: have a burst tyre/have a blowout/get a puncture
definition: <apei>, its wheel, and <kitam.3>, burst: the tyre of a car or an aeroplane bursts; stands after the vehicle, and the meaning is not that of <kitam.2>, be many
<apei> and <kawm> written as one word: the space at or between the wheels of a vehicle, also the inside of a turning wheel
<a> with a word for flat, written as one word: flat in shape, as against {a pum}, round; also a flat piece or plate of something
<a> and <pelh> written as one word: he breaks, of a promise; {kamciam apelh kei} is he does not break his promise
Christian in Rome whom Paul greets as tested and approved in Christ
<a> and the topic marker <pen> written as one word after a noun: as for, marking what the sentence is about
children born together at one birth, usually two; {unau apeng} is twin brothers or sisters
<apeng>, twin, and <ding>, to be, written as one word: the one that was to become a twin
<a> and <pet> written as one word: it bit, or the one that bit, said of a dog, a shark or another animal
Christian woman greeted in the letter of Paul to Philemon
{a pha} written as one word; also stands alone as that which is good

the prefix <a> written together with <pha>, reach: reaching or amounting to, after a number of years, days, storeys or a weight, as in {kum 112 apha}, aged 112, and {inndawl 3 apha}, of three storeys; not {apha}, good
<a> and <phacia> written as one word: its size, how big it is
<a> and <phadawm> written as one word: the one that is better off, it is not so bad
<a> and <phading> written as one word: that comes to about, that is estimated to reach a number, size or weight
<a> and <phak> written as one word: he, she or it reached, of an age or a number of days; {kum 4 aphak ciangin} is when he was 4 years old

terms: until reaching/up to the age of
definition: <a>, <phak>, reach, and <dong>, until, written as one word, after an age or a number: until he or she reached it

<a>, <pha> in the sense reach or amount to, and <khat>, one, written as one word after a number: one that has reached that age, weight or size; {kum 8 aphakhat} is one who is eight years old and {inndawl 4 aphakhat} a building of four floors
<a> and <phakhin> written as one word: who has already reached a number, used in giving an age; {kum 54 aphakhin khat} is one who has reached 54 years
<a>, <phakhin> and <khat> written as one word, after an age in years: a person who has reached that age, as in {kum 45 aphakhinkhat}, a 45-year-old

terms: man aged/the man who has reached
definition: <aphakhin>, having reached, and <pa>, man, written as one word after a number of years: the man who is that old, as in {kum 39 aphakhinpa}, the 39 year old man
<a>, <phakhin> and <pan> written as one word, said of age after <kum> and a number: who has just reached that many years
<a> and <phakhinta> written as one word after a number: an age or a count has now reached that figure
<aphak>, reached, with the marker <in>, written as one word: when he or she reached an age, as in {kum 5 aphakin}, at the age of 5
<a>, <phak> and <khit> written as one word: once he, she or it has reached an age or a number of years, mostly before <ciangin>
<a> and <phakloh> written as one word: not reaching a number or measure; {aphakloh phamawh}, it will not do not to reach, is must reach
<a> and <phal> written as one word: he or it permits, the one that permits; mostly with a negative, as in {aphal nawnlo}, no longer allows
<a> and <phallo> written as one word: he or they do not allow it, or the ones who do not allow it; {zatding aphallo} is they forbid its use
<a>, <phal>, permit, and <loh>, not, written as one word: that is not permitted, what someone does not allow
<a> and <phamawh> written as one word: that matters; after a verb with <loh>, as in {omloh aphamawh}, it means that cannot be left undone or done without
{a pha pan} written as one word, placed after an age in years or months: having just reached that age, only so old

terms: just about so old/about to turn
definition: <aphapan>, just turned, and <ding> written as one word after an age: who would be just about that age, said of an estimated age
<a>, <pha>, reach, <pan>, only just, and <khat>, one, written as one word; after an age, {kum 5 aphapankhat}, one who has only just reached that age

terms: the one reaching/one that amounts to
definition: <apha>, reaching or amounting to, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word after a number or measure: one of that many storeys or that length; not the superlative of <pha>, good, which is written the same
<a> and <phat> written as one word: he praises, they praise, to praise
<a> with a form of <pha> that is spelled like <phat>, used before words such as <teh> and <hun>: when the weather is fine, or on reaching an age or number
<a> and <phate> written as one word: those that have reached a stated age, number or size
<a> and <phattuamna> written as one word: the benefit or good of a thing
<a> and <phawk> written as one word: he remembers or is aware of; {khua aphawk} is be conscious or come to, and {aphawk huai} is worth remembering
<a> and <phawkkhalo> written as one word: he, she or they did not notice, or the one who did not notice
<a> and <phazah> written as one word: how much there is of something, an amount such as some, much or a little that is not given as a counted number
<a> and <phei>, thigh, written as one word: the thigh or leg of the person spoken of
<a> and <pheimal> written as one word: the portion of the leg given nowadays in place of the leg meat
<a> and <pheisa> written as one word: the leg meat of the slaughtered animal
<a>, <phei>, leg, <sa>, meat, and a last part that is taken as strip or slab, written as one word, {a-phei-sa-vo}: a strip of the meat of the leg of a slaughtered animal
<a> and <phelh> written as one word: he or she puts out a fire, or the putting out of it
<aphelh> and <ding> written as one word: in order to put out a fire, mostly followed by <in>

terms: in order to put out/to extinguish
definition: <aphelh> and <dingin> written as one word: in order to put out a fire

terms: have fought the fire/finish putting out
definition: <aphelh> and <khit> written as one word, mostly before <ciangin> or <uhciangin>: after they had worked at putting out the fire
<a>, <phel>, take apart, and <khiat>, out, written as one word before <ciangin>: when it was opened up or taken apart
<a> and <pheng> written as one word, before a verb of speaking: without basis or care, as in {apheng gengawp}, talk wildly
the answer to a question or a problem, and what comes back in return for what is done
<a> and <phi>, sit an examination or an interview, written as one word: he sits it, the one who sits it
placed before a verb of hitting or shooting, usually one with <gawp>: at everyone in the way without choosing, the whole crowd at once
with <thautawh> or <thau> before it: fire a gun at people without aim, shooting whoever is there; the prefix <a>, <phial> and <kap>, shoot, written as one word
<a>, <phial> and <kapgawp> written as one word: he fired in all directions at whoever was there, said of a gunman in a mass shooting
<a> and <phiat> written as one word: he or she sweeps; {inn aphiat} is sweeps the floor
<a> and <phu.1>, revenge, written as one word: revenge for him or for it; {aphu la} is take revenge, avenge
<a> and <phu.2>, push against, written as one word: meet a hardship or an opponent head on
<a> and <phuah> written as one word: that he composed, said of a song, or made up, said of a name
<a> and <phuak> written as one word: he composed a song or gave a name, or the one who composed it
<a> and <phuakte> written as one word: those who composed or made it; {Late aphuakte} is the writers of the Psalms
<a> and <phual> written as one word: the very place where something happened; {aphual ah} is on the spot, at the scene
<aphual>, the very place, and <mahah>, right at: on the spot, at the scene; in reports of accidents and attacks, of a person who dies where it happened

terms: on the spot/at the very place
definition: <aphual>, the scene, and the emphatic <mah> written as one word, followed by <ah>: right there where it happened, as in {aphualmah ah sipah}, died on the spot
<aphual> with <phual> repeated, often after <munmun>: each place in turn, every place where people are
<a> and <phualpi> in the sense main site written as one word: its main plant or central seat, as in {tuihawmkhiatna aphualpi}, the main water distribution plant

terms: on the very spot/right at the scene
definition: <aphual>, the scene, with <zang.2>, the very middle: right at the place where the thing happened; {aphualzang mahah sipah} is died at once on the spot
<a> and <phuankhia> written as one word: the one who founded or started something
<a> and <phugawp> written as one word: of a vehicle or its driver, run hard into something or someone
<a> and <phukha> written as one word: ran into, struck, said mostly of a vehicle; also the one that hit
<a> and <phulgawp> written as one word: it rammed into, drove into with force
<a> and <phulkhia> written as one word: that wells up or comes out from within, said of thoughts, effort or knowledge
<a> and <phum> written as one word: that someone buried, what is laid under the ground
<a> and <phum> written as one word, with <tui>, water: baptizing
<a>, <phum>, bury, and the causative <sak> written as one word: the one who buried someone or had someone buried in the ground
<a>, <phum>, immerse, and the causative <sak> written as one word: the one who pushed something under a liquid
<a> and <phun> written as one word: he grumbles, or one who grumbles
<a> and <phung> written as one word: his or her clan, mostly in the pair {abeh aphung}, his family and clan
<a> and <phunphun> written as one word: the people who keep complaining, or their complaining; often after the words of the complaint and <ci'n>
<a>, <phu.2>, push against, and <suk>, down, written as one word: a vehicle runs into another, here from behind
<a> and <phut> written as one word: he or they found or set up, as in {gam aphut}, found a country
<a> and <phut> written as one word, said of a vehicle: it runs into a person or thing
<a> and <phutkhak> written as one word: what something ran into or collided with, mostly in reports of road accidents; also what one has come up against
<a> and <phutkhakna>, collision, written as one word: the collision of a vehicle, or the spot where it struck
<a> and <phutkhia> written as one word: the one who founded it, he or she founded
<a> with <phut>, run into, and <sak>, written as one word, in road accident reports: a vehicle rams into another, as {anunglam aphutsak}, it rammed into the rear
